title: Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842–1901)
definition: A pioneering Indian social reformer, economist, and judge, often called the 'Father of Indian Economics' and the 'Prince of Graduates', who provided the intellectual foundation for the Indian National Congress.
importanceInUpsc: Ranade is a perennial favorite in Modern History (Social Reform Movements) and GS Paper I (Indian Society). Questions focus on his institutional building, economic critique of British rule, and his role as a mentor to Gokhale.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Mahadev Govind Ranade.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
